prototype_state: local benchmark-only changes layered on source_revision; not production-enabled

method.scenario: synthetic geometry coding escalation (diagnose, then explicit fix)
method.stable_schema_candidate: HADES advertises the same five workspace schemas in diagnosis and action; valid_tool_names allows only read_file and search_files during diagnosis
method.dynamic_baseline: HADES advertises read/search during diagnosis and all five workspace schemas during action

decision: Do not adopt stable schemas as a product fix. In this small fixture, HADES remained about 13.5 seconds slower than PLAIN in both runs; the stable-schema candidate used more HADES model calls and was slightly slower than the dynamic-schema HADES rerun.
limitations: Two repeats per arm are diagnostic; local generation variance is substantial.
Synthetic one-file coding task does not establish broad task quality or owner preference.
PLAIN behavior varied between the two runs, including model API calls and tool results.
This direct AIAgent benchmark does not qualify Open WebUI persistence, deployed gateway authentication, Git commit behavior, or larger coding tasks.
The stable-schema prototype was uncommitted during measurement; the source_revision identifies its base, not the complete experimental tree.
privacy: Metrics only; no prompt/response text, tool arguments, fixture contents, or local paths included.
